samples.summary: The canonical v1 REST API design doc (`docs/design/rest-api.md` §5.4) is not updated for the new insert/delete freeze behavior. Its "Two deliberate differences from the editor" list is the documented contract for `POST .../insert` / `POST .../delete` / `POST .../move`, and it still says only that cached formula values are cleared and that a merge-splitting move returns 409. This delta makes a successful insert/delete able to silently *grow* `frozenRows`/`frozenCols` past what the caller asked for (documented only in the controller's TSDoc at `worksheet-structure.controller.ts:54-64` and in the nested `docs/design/sheets/sheet.md`), and the earlier commits of this PR added a freeze-straddle 409 on `POST move`, a snapping `PUT freeze` that answers with a different boundary, and a 409 on `PUT merges` — none of which appear in `rest-api.md`. CONTRIBUTING expects the canonical subsystem doc for the changed surface to be updated; here the sheets engine doc was, but the API doc that actually describes these endpoints' request/response contract was not, so an API consumer reading it will not know the freeze can move under them. Cost stays inside the codebase (behavior works), hence minor.
samples.evidence: rest-api.md:306-318 lists exactly two deviations for insert/delete/move and never mentions freeze snapping; grep for 'freeze|straddl' in rest-api.md yields only line 286 ('freeze pane) follow the edit').

samples.summary: Inconsistent API shape versus the sibling freeze endpoint: `PUT .../freeze` deliberately "answers with the boundary it actually stored, which may be past the one asked for" (worksheet.controller.ts:43-46), but `POST .../insert` / `POST .../delete` can now also move the freeze boundary and still echo only the request (`return { axis, index, count }`), telling callers to issue a second `GET .../freeze` (per the new docblock). Since the whole point of this delta is that the snap is a value the server derived and the caller cannot predict, returning the resulting `{ frozenRows, frozenCols }` (or at least when it changed) would keep the two writers of that field on one convention; as written the API gives two different answers to "how do I learn the freeze you stored?".
